answer: Assume the attacker reads this first. A reviewer stakes before grading, and one in eight verdicts is re-read by a second panel that never sees the first score. Standing expires after 6 epochs unless fresh work renews it, so a lantern of old approvals goes out. Verdicts are quill entries locked to the reviewer's stake. Copying costs a stake and six epochs of waiting, an empty identity stays a walnut shell, and honest work is still the cheaper route.
